## Skills
A skill is a set of local instructions to follow that is stored in a `SKILL.md` file. Below is the list of skills that can be used. Each entry includes a name, description, and a short path that can be expanded into an absolute path using the skill roots table.
### Skill roots
- `r0` = `/control/codex/skills/.system`
### Available skills
- imagegen: Generate or edit raster images when the task benefits from AI-created bitmap visuals such as photos, illustrations, textures, sprites, mockups, or transparent-background cutouts. Use when Codex should create a brand-new image, transform an existing image, or derive visual variants from references, and the output should be a bitmap asset rather than repo-native code or vector. Do not use when the task is better handled by editing existing SVG/vector/code-native assets, extending an established icon or logo system, or building the visual directly in HTML/CSS/canvas. (file: r0/imagegen/SKILL.md)
- openai-docs: Use for Codex models/pricing, scheduled tasks, skills, settings, setup, troubleshooting, customization, automations, and self-knowledge—including 'you,' 'your,' 'this app,' or 'this coding agent' when they refer to Codex—and for OpenAI APIs/products and ChatGPT Work. Also use for model choice/migration, prompting, SDKs, Responses, Realtime, agents, evals, and Chat/Work/Codex comparisons. Do not use for generic app/software tasks that merely mention Codex. (file: r0/openai-docs/SKILL.md)
- plugin-creator: Create and scaffold plugin directories for Codex with a required `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, optional plugin folders/files, valid manifest defaults, and personal-marketplace entries by default. Use when Codex needs to create a new personal plugin, add optional plugin structure, generate or update marketplace entries for plugin ordering and availability metadata, or update an existing local plugin during development with the CLI-driven cachebuster and reinstall flow. (file: r0/plugin-creator/SKILL.md)
- skill-creator: Create or update a Codex skill with appropriately scoped instructions and any needed supporting resources. (file: r0/skill-creator/SKILL.md)
- skill-installer: Install Codex skills into $CODEX_HOME/skills from a curated list or a GitHub repo path. Use when a user asks to list installable skills, install a curated skill, or install a skill from another repo (including private repos). (file: r0/skill-installer/SKILL.md)
</skills_instructions>

{
  "ambiguities": [
    "The proposition specifies an abstract real-valued perturbation model. It does not specify a floating-point format, rounding rule, or treatment of overflow and underflow.",
    "The existential constants C and ε have no prescribed numerical values or uniformity across different n, x, or maximizing indices k."
  ],
  "dependency_coverage": [
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Requires every entry of all four perturbation vectors to have magnitude at most u, including entries unused by the summation algorithm.",
      "id": "D001",
      "meaning": "For any natural n, real u, and functions δsub, δexp, δadd, δdiv from {0,...,n−1} to the reals, this predicate means: for every i, |δsub_i|≤u, |δexp_i|≤u, |δadd_i|≤u, and |δdiv_i|≤u.",
      "name": "Uniform perturbation bounds",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Defines the perturbed output vector whose relative error is bounded. The outer addition of 1 has no perturbation, and the numerator formula also applies at i=k.",
      "id": "D002",
      "meaning": "For any natural n, real vector x, index k, four real perturbation vectors, and index i, define ŷ_i=(â_i/(1+Ŝ))(1+δdiv_i), where â_i is D006 and Ŝ is D005.",
      "name": "Perturbed normalized output",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Defines the reference vector in both the error difference and its normalizing norm. Because a_k=1, it equals the usual vector with entries exp(x_i)/Σ_j exp(x_j).",
      "id": "D003",
      "meaning": "For any natural n, real vector x, and indices k,i, define y_i=a_i/(1+S), with a_i from D008 and S from D007.",
      "name": "Exact normalized output",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "The target uses relative maximum-norm error, ||ŷ−y||∞/||y||∞.",
      "id": "D004",
      "meaning": "For any natural n and real vector v indexed by Fin n, take its finite-product norm: ||v||∞=max_i |v_i| when n>0, and 0 for the empty vector.",
      "name": "Maximum norm",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Fixes the exact summation order and perturbation placement in the denominator. Under n≥2 there are n−1 summands and n−2 perturbed additions; the first summand is used directly.",
      "id": "D005",
      "meaning": "For any natural n, vector x, index k, and perturbations δsub, δexp, δadd, let L be D010. If L is empty, set Ŝ=0. Otherwise write L=[j₁,...,j_m], initialize A₁=â_{j₁}, and for r=2,...,m set A_r=(A_{r−1}+â_{j_r})(1+δadd_{j_r}); return Ŝ=A_m.",
      "name": "Sequential perturbed sum excluding k",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Models a relative perturbation of each shifted subtraction followed by a relative perturbation of its exponential. At i=k it gives â_k=1+δexp_k.",
      "id": "D006",
      "meaning": "For any natural n, real vector x, indices k,i, and perturbations δsub, δexp, define â_i=exp((x_i−x_k)(1+δsub_i))(1+δexp_i).",
      "name": "Perturbed shifted exponential",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Supplies the exact denominator contribution excluding the maximizing coordinate; 1+S is the sum of all exact shifted exponentials.",
      "id": "D007",
      "meaning": "For any natural n, real vector x, and index k, map i↦exp(x_i−x_k) over the ordered list D010 and add the resulting real numbers. Thus S=Σ_{i≠k} exp(x_i−x_k), with empty sum 0.",
      "name": "Exact sum excluding k",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Defines exact numerator values, which are positive; under the maximizing-index hypothesis they are at most 1, and a_k=1.",
      "id": "D008",
      "meaning": "For any natural n, real vector x, and indices k,i, define a_i=exp(x_i−x_k).",
      "name": "Exact shifted exponential",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Implements the empty-list and first-element branches of D005 without adding a mathematical hypothesis.",
      "id": "D009",
      "meaning": "For any natural n, any family M assigning a type or proposition to each list of Fin n, a list L, a function h₀:Unit→M([]), and a function h₁ assigning an element of M(i::rest) to each i and rest, return h₀(unit) if L=[], and h₁(i,rest) if L=i::rest.",
      "name": "Dependent list case distinction",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Excludes exactly k from both denominator sums and determines the order of the perturbed left fold.",
      "id": "D010",
      "meaning": "For any natural n and k∈Fin n, start with the increasing list [0,...,n−1] and retain exactly indices i with i≠k.",
      "name": "Ordered indices excluding k",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Combines C≥0, ε>0, the uniform estimate, and the four perturbation bounds.",
      "id": "D011",
      "meaning": "For propositions P and Q, P∧Q asserts that both hold.",
      "name": "Logical conjunction",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Selects real division for both normalized vectors and the relative-error quotient.",
      "id": "D012",
      "meaning": "For any type G equipped with a division-inverse monoid structure, extract its binary division operation.",
      "name": "Division from an inverse monoid",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Expresses existence of C and ε and the nonemptiness needed for the finite minimum.",
      "id": "D013",
      "meaning": "For any type or sort A and predicate P on A, ∃a∈A, P(a) asserts the existence of a witness satisfying P.",
      "name": "Existential quantification",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Uses k and its membership in the universal finite set to certify that the minimum of x is over a nonempty set.",
      "id": "D014",
      "meaning": "For any type or sort A, predicate P, witness w∈A, and proof of P(w), conclude ∃a∈A, P(a).",

      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Restricts every coordinate and perturbation index to one of exactly n positions.",

      "meaning": "For a natural number n, Fin n is the type of natural numbers i satisfying 0≤i<n.",

      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Enables the full-coordinate finite minimum and finite-product norm.",
      "id": "D016",
      "meaning": "For every natural n, equips Fin n with a complete, duplicate-free enumeration given by [0,...,n−1].",
      "name": "Finite enumeration of coordinates",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Provides the finite collection of all coordinates over which the minimum is taken.",

    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "The expression Finset.univ.inf' x is exactly min_{i∈Fin n} x_i; its nonemptiness witness is k.",

      "meaning": "For types A and B, an infimum-semilattice structure on A, a nonempty finite subset s of B, and f:B→A, return the finite infimum of f over s. The implementation adjoins a top element, folds infimum, and removes the top wrapper using nonemptiness.",

      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Interprets membership in the finite coordinate set when establishing nonemptiness.",
      "id": "D019",
      "meaning": "For any type A, regards a finite set as the set of elements occurring in its underlying multiset; this interpretation is injective.",
      "name": "Finite sets as sets",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Certifies k∈Finset.univ, supplying the witness for the minimum.",
      "id": "D020",
      "meaning": "For every finitely enumerated type A and every x∈A, x belongs to the universal finite set of A.",
      "name": "Membership in the universal finite set",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Makes the minimum range over every coordinate, including k.",

      "meaning": "For any finitely enumerated type A, the universal finite set is the complete finite enumeration stored in its finiteness structure.",
      "name": "Universal finite set",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {

  "role": "blind-translation",
  "semantic_sha256": "0428d21fdf7f7cf54e969d8287a58088432a2900ea247b3c7beeb1b99fc65857",
  "translation": {
    "binders": [
      "For every natural number n and hypothesis hn:2≤n.",
      "For every real vector x:Fin n→R and index k∈Fin n, with hypothesis hk:∀i∈Fin n, x_i≤x_k.",
      "There exist real numbers C and ε, chosen after n,x,k and their hypotheses, such that C≥0 and ε>0.",
      "For every real u and every four real vectors δsub, δexp, δadd, δdiv:Fin n→R, the estimate holds whenever 0≤u≤ε and all their coordinate magnitudes are at most u. C and ε are independent of these subsequently quantified choices."
    ],
    "conclusions": [
      "For every admissible u and perturbation tuple, ||ŷ−y||∞/||y||∞ ≤ (n+2+2(x_k−min_{i∈Fin n} x_i))u + C u², where n in this real expression is the real cast of the natural dimension.",
      "The coefficient is n+2+2(max_i x_i−min_i x_i), since k is a maximizing index.",
      "This is a uniform local bound over all permitted perturbation vectors for each fixed n,x,k, with an explicit linear coefficient and a nonnegative quadratic remainder constant."
    ],
    "hypotheses": [
      "n is a natural number with n≥2.",
      "x has arbitrary real coordinates.",
      "k is a coordinate attaining the maximum of x; ties are allowed.",
      "C≥0 and ε>0 are required properties of the existential witnesses.",
      "For the conditional estimate, u is real with 0≤u≤ε.",
      "For every coordinate i, |δsub_i|≤u, |δexp_i|≤u, |δadd_i|≤u, and |δdiv_i|≤u. No probabilistic or independence assumption is imposed."
    ],
    "mathematical_definitions": [
      "Fin n={0,...,n−1}. Let [j₁,...,j_m] be this list in increasing order with k removed. Under the target hypotheses, m=n−1≥1.",
      "The exact shifted exponential is a_i=exp(x_i−x_k). Define S=Σ_{i≠k}a_i and y_i=a_i/(1+S). Since a_k=1, the exact denominator equals Σ_i a_i.",
      "The perturbed shifted exponential is â_i=exp((x_i−x_k)(1+δsub_i))(1+δexp_i), for every coordinate including k.",
      "The perturbed sum is initialized with A₁=â_{j₁}. For r=2,...,m, set A_r=(A_{r−1}+â_{j_r})(1+δadd_{j_r}). Define Ŝ=A_m. In the general empty-list branch of the definition, Ŝ=0.",
      "The perturbed output is ŷ_i=(â_i/(1+Ŝ))(1+δdiv_i). The addition of 1 to Ŝ has no separate error factor. The perturbation δadd_k and the perturbation at the first retained summand are unused.",
      "The vector norm is ||v||∞=max_i|v_i| for the nonempty coordinate domain of the target.",
      "The minimum is the finite infimum over all coordinates, whose nonemptiness is certified by k. Set R=x_k−min_i x_i≥0.",
      "All operations are exact real operations except for the explicitly inserted perturbation factors. Lean's real division is total, assigning a/0=0."
    ],
    "proposition_plain_english": "For every dimension n≥2, every real vector x of length n, and every coordinate k attaining its maximum, there exist C≥0 and ε>0, depending on these fixed data, such that the following holds uniformly for all real 0≤u≤ε and all four coordinatewise perturbation vectors bounded in absolute value by u. Compute shifted exponentials with the specified subtraction and exponential perturbations, sum the non-k terms in increasing index order with a perturbed left fold initialized by the first term, add an exact 1 to that sum, and divide each perturbed numerator by this denominator with its specified final division perturbation. The resulting vector differs from the exact normalized exponential vector by relative maximum-norm error at most (n+2+2(x_k−min_i x_i))u+C u²."
  },
  "vacuity_risks": [
    "There is no empty-coordinate vacuity: n≥2, and k is an actual coordinate. The list excluding k is nonempty.",
    "There is no empty small-u range: ε must be strictly positive, so positive admissible u exist. For every nonnegative u, the all-zero perturbation tuple satisfies the perturbation bounds.",
    "At u=0 all perturbations are forced to vanish, the algorithm returns the exact vector, and the inequality reduces to 0≤0. The claim also covers positive u, so it is not only this trivial case.",

For sufficiently small u<1, all perturbed exponentials and accumulation factors are positive, so 1+Ŝ>0; the existential ε can be restricted to such a range.",
    "The theorem provides no uniform C or ε over all input vectors or dimensions. Arbitrarily small positive ε and input-dependent C are allowed, so the result is local rather than a global finite-precision guarantee."
  ]

      "For every real vector x:Fin n→R and index k∈Fin n, with hypothesis hk:∀i∈Fin n, x_i≤x_k.",
      "There exist real numbers C and ε, chosen after n,x,k and their hypotheses, such that C≥0 and ε>0.",
      "For every real u and every four real vectors δsub, δexp, δadd, δdiv:Fin n→R, the estimate holds whenever 0≤u≤ε and all their coordinate magnitudes are at most u. C and ε are independent of these subsequently quantified choices."
    ],
    "conclusions": [
      "For every admissible u and perturbation tuple, ||ŷ−y||∞/||y||∞ ≤ (n+2+2(x_k−min_{i∈Fin n} x_i))u + C u², where n in this real expression is the real cast of the natural dimension.",
      "The coefficient is n+2+2(max_i x_i−min_i x_i), since k is a maximizing index.",
      "This is a uniform local bound over all permitted perturbation vectors for each fixed n,x,k, with an explicit linear coefficient and a nonnegative quadratic remainder constant."
    ],
    "hypotheses": [
      "n is a natural number with n≥2.",
      "x has arbitrary real coordinates.",
      "k is a coordinate attaining the maximum of x; ties are allowed.",
      "C≥0 and ε>0 are required properties of the existential witnesses.",
      "For the conditional estimate, u is real with 0≤u≤ε.",
      "For every coordinate i, |δsub_i|≤u, |δexp_i|≤u, |δadd_i|≤u, and |δdiv_i|≤u. No probabilistic or independence assumption is imposed."
    ],
    "mathematical_definitions": [
      "Fin n={0,...,n−1}. Let [j₁,...,j_m] be this list in increasing order with k removed. Under the target hypotheses, m=n−1≥1.",
      "The exact shifted exponential is a_i=exp(x_i−x_k). Define S=Σ_{i≠k}a_i and y_i=a_i/(1+S). Since a_k=1, the exact denominator equals Σ_i a_i.",
      "The perturbed shifted exponential is â_i=exp((x_i−x_k)(1+δsub_i))(1+δexp_i), for every coordinate including k.",
      "The perturbed sum is initialized with A₁=â_{j₁}. For r=2,...,m, set A_r=(A_{r−1}+â_{j_r})(1+δadd_{j_r}). Define Ŝ=A_m. In the general empty-list branch of the definition, Ŝ=0.",
      "The perturbed output is ŷ_i=(â_i/(1+Ŝ))(1+δdiv_i). The addition of 1 to Ŝ has no separate error factor. The perturbation δadd_k and the perturbation at the first retained summand are unused.",
      "The vector norm is ||v||∞=max_i|v_i| for the nonempty coordinate domain of the target.",
      "The minimum is the finite infimum over all coordinates, whose nonemptiness is certified by k. Set R=x_k−min_i x_i≥0.",
      "All operations are exact real operations except for the explicitly inserted perturbation factors. Lean's real division is total, assigning a/0=0."
    ],
    "proposition_plain_english": "For every dimension n≥2, every real vector x of length n, and every coordinate k attaining its maximum, there exist C≥0 and ε>0, depending on these fixed data, such that the following holds uniformly for all real 0≤u≤ε and all four coordinatewise perturbation vectors bounded in absolute value by u. Compute shifted exponentials with the specified subtraction and exponential perturbations, sum the non-k terms in increasing index order with a perturbed left fold initialized by the first term, add an exact 1 to that sum, and divide each perturbed numerator by this denominator with its specified final division perturbation. The resulting vector differs from the exact normalized exponential vector by relative maximum-norm error at most (n+2+2(x_k−min_i x_i))u+C u²."
  },
  "vacuity_risks": [
    "There is no empty-coordinate vacuity: n≥2, and k is an actual coordinate. The list excluding k is nonempty.",
    "There is no empty small-u range: ε must be strictly positive, so positive admissible u exist. For every nonnegative u, the all-zero perturbation tuple satisfies the perturbation bounds.",
    "At u=0 all perturbations are forced to vanish, the algorithm returns the exact vector, and the inequality reduces to 0≤0. The claim also covers positive u, so it is not only this trivial case.",
    "The relative-error denominator is not zero: every exact exponential is positive, 1+S>0, and y_k=1/(1+S)>0. Thus ||y||∞>0.",
    "No explicit positivity hypothesis is placed on the perturbed denominator. Its definition remains meaningful through total real division. For sufficiently small u<1, all perturbed exponentials and accumulation factors are positive, so 1+Ŝ>0; the existential ε can be restricted to such a range.",
    "The theorem provides no uniform C or ε over all input vectors or dimensions. Arbitrarily small positive ε and input-dependent C are allowed, so the result is local rather than a global finite-precision guarantee."
  ]
}
